To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multidrug resistant Enteroccus faecium strains isolated from poultry samples and hospitals in Michigan and Florida were resistant to the last alternative antibiotic used to treat VRE in clinical settings.
the multidrug resistant enterococci originating from farm animals have the ability to proliferate at a substantial pace and could reach hospitals.
the MEF strains collected in the poultry retail outlets in Ann Arbor, Michigan area were resistant to the last alternative antibiotic, quinuprisin/dalfoprisin (QD).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of MDR Enterococci in poultry and the possibility of their transfer to clinical settings.
the presence and distribution of multidrug resistant E. faccium in the food chain that could impact the health of the general public.
the emergence of multidrug resistance in E. faecim strains that can impact food chains and hospitals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
poultry and clinical strains are resistant to the last alternative antibiotic used to treat VRE infections.
the poultry industry is a reservoir for MEF strains that are resistant to the last alternative antibiotic QD.
MEF strains isolated from poultry samples were multidrug resistant to all the drugs tested and were also resistant to QDs, the last alternative drugs used to treat VRE infections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the poultry samples were contaminated by MEF strains and these strains could have been transmitted to the clinical setting and vice versa.
the MEF isolates are present in poultry products and are resistant to all the antibiotics used in the hospitals.
poultry is a reservoir for MEF strains which are multidrug resistant and can be transmitted to humans via food chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MEF strains are proliferating at an alarming rate in food chains and could be transmitted to hospitals and other healthcare settings.
MEF strains are emerging as a major threat to human health and could be a source of VRE strains in the hospitals.
the MEF strains are resistant to QD and are present in food animals and in hospitals, and therefore, could be transmitted to humans.
